note: Item text is INEP's own, from the accessibility booklet, chosen as the primary source because INEP wrote verbal descriptions of figures, graphs and tables into it: 51 stems and 5 option rows carry an INEP-authored description. Booklet position -> IRW item via ITENS_PROVA_2023.csv for CO_PROVA 1207, so item values are the publisher's own and never reconstructed. No ENEM item shares a passage with another (verified four ways: no shared-passage markers, no question lacking its own stem, no adjacent stems >45% similar, no long sentence in two stems), so section_id is the trivial <table>_1 and section_prompt is empty. Administered in Portuguese; the deposit contains no English version (checked: only data dictionaries and SAS/SPSS/R import scripts), so the _translated columns were produced by this project. raw_resp carries the printed option letter A-E: the live tables have a `text` column holding that raw letter, so without it option_text could not be joined to text=='A' and the four distractors would be anonymous. Rows are in A-E order. All 50 items from the accessibility booklet. The 50-items-for-45-positions count is the foreign-language block: positions 1-5 appear twice, disambiguated by TP_LINGUA (0=English, 1=Spanish) and by the booklet's explicit '(opcao ingles)'/'(opcao espanhol)' headers. The REDACAO essay prompt trailing the objective questions is not an item in the response table and is not shipped. Four items (140595, 140736, 140959, 15035) carry INEP's own '[supressao de texto]' where copyrighted stimulus was withheld at source. TRANSLATION: five items have an English stimulus and five a Spanish one; those stimuli are the object of study and are kept verbatim in the _translated columns rather than round-tripped, per language_backfill/README.md. Where options analyse specific Spanish or Portuguese words (141707, 141814), the quoted word is kept in the original with an English gloss.
public_note: Item text is INEP's own accessibility-booklet wording, including its descriptions of figures. The English in the *_translated columns was produced by this project, not by INEP. In the foreign-language items the English or Spanish stimulus is kept verbatim rather than translated, and four items carry INEP's own marker where copyrighted stimulus was withheld from the published booklet.
